articles.title: uSMART and PIVOT Fintech Introduce GlobalSave Portfolios Balanced Strategy on FollowSmart
articles.description: SINGAPORE, Oct. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- uSMART Securities (Singapore) Pte. Ltd. ("uSMART") has announced the addition of the PIVOT- GlobalSave Portfolios Balanced Strategy to its FollowSmart platform. Managed by PIVOT Fintech Pte. Ltd. ("PIVOT"), the strategy is being made available through uSMART's digital platform as part of the companies' collaboration to provide investors with access to professionally managed investment strategies. Investors can find information about available strategies via the uSMART App at uSMART Securities. Streamlining Operations for Fund Management Companies Offering professionally managed investment strategies to a wider investor base can involve significant technology, operational and client servicing requirements. FollowSmart provides a digital workflow supporting account onboarding, trade implementation, position monitoring, valuation and client reporting. The platform is designed to help investment managers handle these operational processes while focusing on portfolio management. Empowering Investors with a Digital Marketplace For individual investors, FollowSmart provides a digital platform for exploring professionally managed investment strategies. Available strategies span different asset classes, global markets and risk profiles. Users can review information such as investment philosophy, historical performance and the credentials of the management team, and monitor their portfolios over time. These features may help investors assess which available strategies are relevant to their own objectives and circumstances. Overview of PIVOT Fintech’s GlobalSave Portfolios Balanced Strategy, available through FollowSmart on the uSMART app. The PIVOT- GlobalSave Portfolios Balanced Strategy uSMART is acting as an authorized distributor of the PIVOT- GlobalSave Portfolios Balanced Strategy, which is managed by MAS-regulated PIVOT Fintech. The investment team is led by Victor Lye. The strategy uses a quantitative investment approach informed by Modern Portfolio Theory (MPT). It invests in U.S.-listed ETFs across equities, fixed income, commodities and real estate to build globally diversified portfolios. Asset allocation weights are adjusted in response to macroeconomic trends, with the objective of balancing expected returns and risk for medium- to long-term investors. Victor Lye, Founder of PIVOT Fintech and Investment Team Lead. Expanding the FollowSmart Ecosystem The addition of PIVOT Fintech is part of uSMART's ongoing development of the FollowSmart platform and its network of investment managers. Other strategies recently added to the platform include the Global Quantitative Core Growth Strategy by Sunova Capital Management and the JMC Absolute Return Strategy by JMC Capital Asset Management. Together, these offerings provide investors with access to a range of professionally managed investment approaches. About uSMART Securities (Singapore) Pte Ltd - uSMART Securities (Singapore) Pte Ltd, established on March 22, 2021, is the Singapore entity under uSMART Group (uSmart Holding Ltd.). The company holds a Capital Markets Services (CMS) Licence (Licence No. CMS101161) regulated by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS). Based in Singapore, it provides financial services through the uSMART platform. Its products include US, Hong Kong, Singapore, Japan and UK stocks, options, futures, ETFs, funds, Contracts for Difference (CFDs) and forex products. Its services include trading tools, client account services, risk management arrangements and segregated client fund accounts. About PIVOT Fintech - PIVOT Fintech Pte. Ltd. (UEN 201716150D) holds a Capital Markets Services Licence (CMS100806) regulated by the Monetary Authority of Singapore and serves as the Investment Manager of the Strategy. PIVOT's investment team is led by its founder, Victor Lye, who has over 35 years of senior leadership experience across wealth management, insurance, fintech, and artificial intelligence. He holds a First-Class Honours Degree in Economics and Accounting from the University of Adelaide and is a Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) and Certified Financial Planner (CFP). articles.title: Nikkei slips, bounces, as Iran oil fears weigh; ING sees BOJ holding at 1.25%, two hikes in 2027
articles.description: Oil is the dominant risk for Japanese assets near term: as a major energy importer, Japan is exposed to any further rise in crude tied to the Iran conflict, which would pressure corporate margins and the trade balance and keep the yen soft near 157 per dollar. A sustained climb in oil would also reinforce imported inflation, complicating the BOJ’s preference to wait and potentially pulling hike expectations forward from January. With a hold fully priced, the yen and JGB yields are likely to react to guidance rather than the decision, and a more hawkish tone could offer the currency some relief. Tech and chip-related names remain the most sensitive part of the market to risk-off swings driven by Middle East headlines. --- Tokyo stocks are trading at the mercy of Middle East headlines and oil, while the BOJ is expected to sit tight this week and save its next moves for the new year. Summary: The Nikkei Stock Average fell about 0.5% to around 62,400, with semiconductor and electronics shares leading declines amid concerns over the Iran conflict and higher energy costs Advantest fell 1.7% and Murata Manufacturing slipped 1.0%; the dollar held around 157 yen, little changed from Friday’s Tokyo close Investors are watching Middle East developments and crude after oil hit a five-month high on Friday ING expects the BOJ to keep its policy rate at 1.25% this week as it assesses last month’s hike, with 25bp increases in January and April 2027 taking the rate to 1.75% ING says policymakers may want more time to monitor the economy as government support for domestic demand continues, leaving the focus on tone and messaging Tokyo October CPI is expected to show headline inflation steady and core easing slightly; September retail sales and industrial production are also due Japanese shares moved lower on Monday as worries about the Iran conflict and rising energy costs continued to weigh on sentiment, with technology stocks bearing the brunt of the selling. The Nikkei Stock Average fell about 0.5% to around 62,400, led by declines in semiconductor and other electronics shares. Chip testing equipment maker Advantest dropped 1.7%, while electronic components producer Murata Manufacturing lost 1.0%. In currency markets, the dollar traded around 157 yen, little changed from levels at Friday’s Tokyo stock market close. Investors are keeping a close eye on developments in the Middle East and on crude oil, after oil prices climbed to their highest level in five months on Friday. For an economy heavily dependent on imported energy, elevated oil prices raise costs for businesses and households alike, and market participants are likely to stay cautious until there is greater clarity on the conflict’s direction. Turning to monetary policy, the Bank of Japan is expected to keep its policy rate unchanged at 1.25% at its meeting this week as it gauges the effects of last month’s rate increase, according to ING economists. Their base case assumes two further 25 basis point hikes, in January and April 2027, which would lift the policy rate to 1.75%. ING noted that while inflation remains elevated, policymakers may prefer to take more time to monitor the economy, particularly as the government continues to support domestic demand. With markets already pricing a hold, the bank said attention will centre on the tone of the BOJ’s messaging and on a fresh round of economic data. Those releases include Tokyo inflation figures for October, where consensus, according to ING, expects headline CPI to hold steady year on year and core inflation to ease slightly. Nationwide retail sales and industrial production data for September are also due. Taken together, the BOJ’s guidance and the incoming data are likely to shape expectations for how soon the next rate hike arrives. This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.
